faq.q: Besides years, months and days, what else does it show?
faq.a: After you pick a date of birth it fills a grid with total months, weeks, days, hours and minutes lived, the weekday you were born on, days until your next birthday and the weekday that birthday falls on. It also derives your Western zodiac, birthstone for your birth month, and Chinese zodiac animal from the birth year.

faq.q: How does the Exam Eligibility Checker handle a cutoff date?
faq.a: You enter a cutoff date plus a minimum and maximum age. It computes your completed years, months and days as on that cutoff, converts it to a decimal age (years + months/12 + days/365), and marks you eligible or not. It shows how far you are inside or past the upper limit, and notes informational relaxations (OBC +3, SC/ST +5) to verify against the official notification.

faq.q: Does it remember dates I have already checked?
faq.a: Yes. Your last date of birth is restored on your next visit, and each date you calculate is kept in a short history list (up to 10 and 12 entries depending on the list) stored only in your browser. Click any saved entry to reload it. You can also download or copy an age report of the current result.

faq.q: How does the Retirement Countdown work?
faq.a: Enter a retirement age (default 60) and it uses the date of birth above to build a retirement date — birth year plus the whole-number part of that age, same month and day. It then shows the date, the years/months/days remaining, and total days left. If that date has already passed, it tells you so instead of showing a countdown.
